title: First Motive machine identity card
description: The one file that says what this machine is. Every other host-level fact — the ROS namespace, the zenoh profile, the compose environment, the systemd unit names, the workspace path — is derived from these fields rather than typed a second time somewhere else. Written by `fm machine init`, or by cloud-init on a flashed card. Read by fm-tools, fm-ros2, fm-comms, fm-docker, and fm-desktop.

schema_version.description: Bumped when a field changes meaning or disappears. A reader that does not know this version must refuse the file rather than guess at it.

name.description: The machine's identity across the fleet: its hostname, its mDNS name, its tailnet name, and the stem its ROS namespace is derived from. Shaped fm-<role-abbrev>-<nn> so two recorders on one LAN cannot collide, which the old singular fm-jetson could not express.

role.description: Which kind of machine this is. Selects the provisioning step list, the ROS distro, and the Ubuntu release fm-setup will accept. `mac` and `robot` are provisioned by neither role — a laptop still needs an identity to point at a workspace and pick a transport, and a robot arrives on its vendor's own OS, adopted by `fm device adopt` rather than flashed.

fleet.description: Which population this machine belongs to. Machines only ever discover, sync with, and update alongside machines in the same fleet, so a rig on a bench cannot be adopted by the production fleet by accident.

transport.description: The middleware profile every process on this host sources. `zenoh` is the supported path; `dds-lan` is the labelled escape hatch kept for hardware that has not been through the transport migration.

workload.description: What this machine does in the stack, when it does one of the things that has a middleware profile. Optional, because it is genuinely not universal: a machine that runs no bridge needs no value, and a required field would force a meaningless one onto it. Absent means this machine hosts no workload. Present, it selects the comms bridge profile — the last per-host value that was still being typed into an env file, because `role` cannot tell a recorder rig from a processor rig when both are `jetson`. `router` is the exception that runs no bridge: it runs zenohd, the one process the whole fleet connects to. It is a workload and not a role because the machine hosting it is an ordinary mac or workstation that also does other work. `cockpit` is a Mac, whose bridge is the mirror of a rig's, and `workstation` is the GPU tower, whose bridge is the union of `robot` and `processor` because it runs both.

robot.description: Which robot this machine is. Required on the `robot` role and absent on every other, because it is the field the rest of the fleet reads to know what it is talking to: fm-comms selects the anvil bridge profile from it, and the robot agent selects its adapter from it. `role` cannot answer that — an Anvil workcell and an Axol are both robots and share not one interface.

workspace.description: Absolute path to the single parent directory holding every First Motive checkout on this machine. Readers must take the workspace from here and never assume a path: a hardcoded ~/fm_ros2 is what this field exists to delete. Absent on a client-mode machine, which has no workspace at all — such a machine has no identity card either.
